payload.title: Daniell cell: reversible EMF and conducting paths

model.title: Daniell cell: reversible EMF and conducting paths
model.description: Unqualified teaching-model proposal for human review. Steady Nernst prediction plus shared qualitative-flow gating; no current or transient simulation.
assumptions: Fixed teaching temperature T=298.15 K; rounded conventional standard cell potential E°cell=1.10 V; electron-transfer number n=2.
R=8.314462618 J/(mol·K), F=96485.33212 C/mol. The voltage coefficient RT/(2F)=0.01284628956 V is precomputed because mol-based units are unavailable.
Concentration controls use dimensionless activities a≈c/c°, with c°=1 mol/L. Each defaults to 1 and ranges independently from 0.001 to 1, corresponding to 0.001–1 mol/L.
Pure zinc and copper solids have unit activity. Concentrations are externally maintained; ideal activities are an approximation, increasingly unrealistic at higher ionic strengths.

Illustrative materials are ZnSO4 and CuSO4 solutions and a KNO3 salt bridge, not learner-specified materials. Sulfate is a spectator; bridge nitrate migrates toward zinc and potassium toward copper during discharge.
Zinc oxidation: Zn(s) → Zn²⁺(aq)+2e⁻. Copper reduction: Cu²⁺(aq)+2e⁻ → Cu(s). Net: Zn(s)+Cu²⁺(aq) → Zn²⁺(aq)+Cu(s).
Within all permitted concentrations, zinc is the negative anode and copper the positive cathode. External electrons travel from zinc to copper, never through electrolyte or bridge.
Wire and bridge inputs are binary and default to 1. Mode is binary: 0=high-impedance EMF measurement, 1=illustrative discharge; default 0.
Measurement uses separate high-impedance leads across the electrodes. The wire switch controls a separately labelled illustrative discharge path, not a current loop through the voltmeter.
Every sustained-flow indicator uses sustained_flow_enabled: discharge mode AND wire connected AND bridge present. Measurement mode shows no sustained-flow animation.
EMF measurement eligibility requires measurement mode and the bridge present. With the bridge removed, the thermodynamic prediction remains visible but is not presented as a measured voltage.
All displayed mode-dependent parts and readouts must use the same declared mode and continuity outputs. Qualitative animation speed carries no quantitative meaning.
limitations: This proposal is not scientifically qualified or product-specific.
No current, load resistance, power, discharge rate, electrode mass-change rate, kinetics or transport calculation is provided.
No switching transients, charge-separation dynamics, depletion, activity coefficients, complexation, precipitation or junction potentials are modeled.
A connected illustrative discharge path permits qualitative flow only; reversible EMF is not a prediction of loaded terminal voltage.
The removed-bridge terminal voltage is outside reliable model scope. Opening the discharge wire does not force composition-based reversible EMF to zero.
Reaction energetics, local electroneutrality, ionic conduction and part roles receive qualitative explanations, not spatial electrochemical calculations.
Steady model only; no analytic time experiment or quantitative animation dynamics.

snapshot.unfinished_question: How does a Daniell cell turn a chemical reaction into electricity? Build an interactive CBSE Class 12 electrochemistry setup with visible zinc and copper half-cells, solutions, a salt bridge, an external wire and a voltmeter. Let me inspect each part, change zinc-ion and copper-ion concentrations, open the wire and remove the salt bridge. Show the correct electron and ion directions, zinc oxidation and copper reduction. Calculate the reversible EMF with the Nernst equation at standard room temperature using the standard cell potential and concentrations as an ideal activity approximation. State all numerical constants and assumptions. Distinguish qualitative flow animation from any calculated current; the open circuit or removed bridge must stop sustained flow. Include guided comparisons and a part-by-part visual explanation.

limits: Layout contains 15 visible, inspectable parts; no elapsed-time simulation.
Visual dimensions are illustrative: one scene unit represents approximately 2 cm of apparatus, not a calculated electrochemical length.
Teaching materials: ZnSO4 and CuSO4 solutions with a KNO3 bridge; sulfate is a spectator ion.
Zn(s) → Zn²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻; Cu²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻ → Cu(s). Net: Zn(s) + Cu²⁺(aq) → Zn²⁺(aq) + Cu(s).
Zinc is the negative anode and copper the positive cathode throughout the supported range. Electrons travel externally from zinc to copper, never through solution.
Nitrate moves toward zinc and potassium toward copper through the bridge, helping maintain local electrical neutrality.

All three separate directional indicators must use sustained_flow_enabled directly, with opacity covering its full 0–1 domain. Opening the wire, removing the bridge or selecting measurement mode hides all three.

Discharge-wire visibility uses wire_connected; removable-bridge visibility uses bridge_present, each over its full 0–1 domain. The independent meter leads remain connected across the electrodes. No bindings or animations are installed at this layout stage; bridge indicators must not inherit a second opacity gate from the bridge themselves. Indicators are qualitative directions, not currents or ion

parts.label: Zinc half-cell vessel
parts.explanation: This clear beaker holds the zinc electrode and its solution. A half-cell is one side of the cell's chemical reaction.

parts.label: ZnSO4 solution
parts.explanation: This solution contains zinc ions and sulfate ions. Sulfate is a spectator: it carries charge but is unchanged in the net reaction.

parts.label: Zinc anode (−)
parts.explanation: Zinc atoms become zinc ions and release electrons: Zn → Zn²⁺ + 2e⁻. This loss of electrons is oxidation.

parts.label: Copper half-cell vessel
parts.explanation: This clear beaker holds the copper electrode and its solution. It keeps this half-cell separate from the zinc solution.

parts.label: CuSO4 solution
parts.explanation: This blue solution contains copper ions and spectator sulfate ions. Copper ions can gain electrons at the copper electrode.

parts.label: Copper cathode (+)
parts.explanation: Copper ions gain electrons here: Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu. This gain of electrons is reduction.

parts.label: Removable KNO3 salt bridge
parts.explanation: This bridge lets ions carry charge between the solutions, helping prevent charge buildup. Electrons do not pass through it.

parts.label: External discharge wire
parts.explanation: This separate path lets electrons travel from zinc to copper when the switch is closed in discharge mode. Its flow arrows do not measure current.

parts.label: Discharge switch
parts.explanation: This switch opens or closes the discharge path. Opening it stops every sustained-flow indicator, but does not make the reversible EMF prediction zero.

parts.label: High-impedance voltmeter
parts.explanation: This meter compares electrode potentials while drawing negligible current. It is not the discharge path or a model of loaded voltage.

parts.label: Zinc meter lead
parts.explanation: This lead joins the zinc electrode to the meter's negative terminal. It stays separate from the switched discharge wire.

parts.label: Copper meter lead
parts.explanation: This lead joins the copper electrode to the meter's positive terminal. Together the meter leads allow a nearly open-circuit comparison.

parts.label: Electrons: zinc → copper
parts.explanation: This arrow points right along the external discharge wire. It shows a qualitative direction, not a calculated current or particle speed.

parts.label: NO3⁻ → zinc
parts.explanation: This bridge arrow points left toward the zinc solution. Nitrate ions help balance the positive charge added as zinc dissolves; the arrow gives no rate.

parts.label: K⁺ → copper
parts.explanation: This bridge arrow points right toward the copper solution. Potassium ions help balance charge as copper ions are consumed; the arrow gives no rate.

experiments.title: Lower zinc-ion concentration
experiments.prompt: Start with both concentrations at 1 mol/L. Predict whether lowering zinc ions to 0.01 mol/L raises or lowers reversible EMF.
experiments.explanation: Lower zinc activity reduces Q=aZn/aCu. Since Erev=1.10 V−0.01284628956 V ln(Q), the reversible prediction increases.

experiments.title: Lower copper-ion concentration
experiments.prompt: Reset both concentrations to 1 mol/L. Predict how lowering copper ions to 0.01 mol/L changes reversible EMF.
experiments.explanation: Lower copper activity increases Q and lowers reversible EMF. These independent concentration settings use ideal activities, not an ionic-strength correction.

experiments.title: Interrupt the electronic path
experiments.prompt: Select illustrative discharge with wire and bridge present. Predict which arrows disappear when you open the wire, and whether reversible EMF changes.
experiments.explanation: Opening the wire sets wire_connected to zero and disables all three directional indicators through the shared gate. The composition-based EMF remains unchanged.

experiments.title: Interrupt the ionic path
experiments.prompt: Reconnect the wire in discharge mode. Predict what happens to all three arrows when you remove the bridge. Then compare measurement mode.
experiments.explanation: Removing the bridge disables every flow indicator without zeroing reversible EMF. Measurement mode also hides all three; a removed-bridge measured voltage is outside model scope.

controls.help: Sets aZn≈cZn/c° with c°=1 mol/L; increasing it lowers reversible EMF. Ideal activities become less realistic at higher ionic strengths.
Sets aCu≈cCu/c° with c°=1 mol/L; increasing it raises reversible EMF. Concentrations are externally maintained.
Opens or connects the separate discharge wire; opening it hides all flow arrows without changing reversible EMF or meter leads.
Removes or restores the ionic bridge; removal hides all flow arrows but preserves the composition-based reversible EMF prediction.
Measurement hides all flow arrows; illustrative discharge enables them only with both paths intact. Neither mode calculates current.

coverage.explanation: Inspect labelled parts for their roles, materials and connections. Separate meter leads distinguish high-impedance measurement from the switched discharge path.

Part explanations connect zinc oxidation and copper reduction to chemical-to-electrical energy conversion. Electrons point externally toward copper; nitrate points toward zinc and potassium toward copper. Directions are qualitative, not transport calculations.
Independent positive activities determine Q and the fixed-temperature Nernst prediction. Comparisons retain T=298.15 K, n=2, E°=1.10 V, R=8.314462618 J/(mol·K), F=96485.33212 C/mol and c°=1 mol/L.

The displayed derived flags feed shared continuity logic. Every arrow's opacity uses sustained_flow_enabled directly: discharge mode AND wire connected AND bridge present. Any interrupted path or measurement mode hides all three.

Arrows indicate direction only, not current or speed. Reversible EMF is not loaded terminal voltage. Pure solids have unit activity; concentrations are maintained. Depletion, nonideal activities, junction potentials, kinetics and switching transients are excluded; removed-bridge measured voltage is outside reliable scope.

outcomes: Inspect labelled zinc and copper electrodes, their electrolyte solutions, a salt bridge, an external wire and a voltmeter, with explanations of each role and connection.
Connect zinc oxidation and copper reduction to chemical-to-electrical energy conversion; distinguish electron transport through the wire from ionic transport through solutions and the bridge.
Vary zinc-ion and copper-ion concentrations independently and compare reversible EMF predictions using the Nernst equation and an ideal-activity approximation.
Compare connected, open-wire and removed-bridge configurations; stop sustained-flow indicators whenever either conducting path is interrupted.
Distinguish qualitative flow animation and reversible EMF from calculated current or an actual loaded terminal voltage; state constants, assumptions and limitations explicitly.

scene_revision.feedback: Preserve the accepted Nernst equations, constants, input ranges and continuity logic. The previous scene had apparatus but no visible charge-flow indicators, despite claiming them. Rebuild a compact two-beaker Daniell apparatus with correctly connected zinc/copper electrodes, separate high-impedance voltmeter leads, switched discharge wire and removable KNO3 salt bridge. Include THREE distinct inspectable flow-indicator parts: electrons pointing from zinc (left) to copper (right) ON THE EXTERNAL WIRE; nitrate ions pointing toward the zinc half-cell through the salt bridge; potassium ions pointing toward copper through the bridge. Use visible directional arrow meshes, with opacity axis all from 0 to 1 driven DIRECTLY by sustained_flow_enabled on every indicator. Do not show electrons in solution. Arrows are qualitative indicators, not calculated currents or particle speeds; explain this. Opening wire, removing bridge or measurement mode must hide ALL three flow indicators while the reversible EMF prediction remains. Use wire_connected and bridge_present for wire/bridge visibility. Keep indicator geometry separate and labelled, full node bounds, real shared connections, modest part count, no time dynamics invented. Provide concentration presets, open/closed controls and guided comparisons.
